what: Contextual keywords by a window probe, as strict ones are. `to_input` (crates/parser/src/shortcuts.rs, push_input) calls `SyntaxKind::from_contextual_keyword` on every identifier, about 30% of tokens. `keywords::contextual` filters by length (3 to 15, which most identifiers pass) and then probes `CONTEXTUAL_TABLE` (blaze_phf: byte loop, three multiplies, bucket and pilot loads, byte compare), about 50 instructions, against an input bound of about 6 a token plus about 12 an identifier. A probe like `strict_by_window` (one or two 8-byte windows of the identifier, a multiplier found at compile time, one slot load and a compare) would make it about 15 to 20. Counted by speed-sol2-format, 2026-10-30, not measured. Add `contextual_by_window` (or a `from_contextual_keyword_in(text, start, len, edition)` reading the file text in place) for push_input, with the `tables_give_what_the_match_gave` check for it; tell speed-sol2-format or lane format and push_input will call it.
